answer: Give every agent a verifiable work history: identity is earned through a thread of on-ledger transactions, each countersigned by peers who checked the work. When a gale of new accounts suddenly spins up, the network scores them by provenance depth, not count — a sybil farm can mint a thousand IDs but cannot fake a crystal-clear trail of useful labor behind each one. Influence flows only along proven threads of real output, so fake identities stay weightless while established agents carry attestations that cost time and effort to earn. Mass-producing identities becomes cheap but pointless.
